newsitem.title: JAPAN: Gajoen Kanko lifted by buyers after profit.
newsitem.headline: Gajoen Kanko lifted by buyers after profit.

text.p: Shares in Gajoen Kanko KK rose in Tuesday afternoon trade, lifted by buyers hoping to obtain short-term profits from the speculative, incentive-backed share, brokers said.
The shares stood 15 yen higher at 113 yen at 0434 GMT.
Gajoen was the third most heavily traded issue in the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange with a volume of 5.955 million shares.

"Most of the market believes that after the elections, trade in incentive-backed speculative shares will make way for issues with solid reasons to buy or sell on," a broker at a medium-sized brokerage said.
"Speculative buyers are trying to rake in profits before the market mood changes," he added.
Other speculative shares such as Keisei Electric and Sansui Electric were traded heavily.
Tokai Kogyo topped the list for largest percentage gains at 610 yen, higher by 80 yen. Trade volume was a modest 421,000 shares.
